04 / 05 — REFLECTIONS

Learning Beyond
the Map.

A reflection on the technologies, analytical methods, and spatial thinking shaping my journey in Geoinformatics.

01

Advanced Remote Sensing

Studying Advanced Remote Sensing helped me understand how different sensing technologies reveal information about the Earth beyond what is visible to the human eye. Exploring SAR, LiDAR, hyperspectral imaging, and UAV-based remote sensing strengthened my understanding of their principles and applications. My hands-on experience with ESA SNAP introduced me to SAR data processing and interpretation. I particularly appreciated learning how these technologies can support urban mapping, vegetation analysis, biomass estimation, and environmental monitoring. This subject encouraged me to look beyond satellite images and understand the physical processes behind the data.

LEARNING TOPICS

  • Active and passive microwave remote sensing
  • SLAR and SAR systems
  • LiDAR remote sensing
  • Hyperspectral remote sensing
  • UAV-based remote sensing
  • SAR data processing using ESA SNAP
02

Geospatial Big Data Analysis

Geospatial Big Data Analysis helped me connect remote sensing data with programming, machine learning, and spatial problem-solving. Working with Google Earth Engine, Python libraries, satellite time series, and precipitation datasets improved my ability to process and interpret large geospatial datasets. Exploring supervised classification, the Segment Anything Model, and data fusion showed me how computational techniques can reveal patterns that are difficult to identify through visual interpretation alone. I gained a stronger appreciation for reproducible workflows and effective data visualization, which I hope to apply to urban and environmental challenges.

LEARNING TOPICS

  • Google Earth Engine
  • Python, GeoPandas, and Shapely
  • Geospatial data mining
  • Supervised classification and the Segment Anything Model
  • MODIS NDVI time-series analysis
  • CHIRPS and GPM precipitation and cyclone mapping
  • Remote sensing data fusion
  • Geospatial big data visualization
03

Techniques in Geospatial Database Management

Learning Geospatial Database Management helped me understand the importance of organizing spatial data efficiently and maintaining its accuracy and accessibility. Through PostgreSQL and PostGIS, I explored spatial database creation, coordinate reference systems, SQL queries, vector and raster data management, and spatial indexing. These concepts helped me recognize that effective GIS analysis depends not only on maps and tools but also on a well-structured data foundation. I see these skills as essential for building scalable geospatial workflows and managing complex datasets for urban planning and environmental applications.

LEARNING TOPICS

  • PostgreSQL and PostGIS
  • Spatial database creation using graphical interfaces and SQL
  • Coordinate reference systems
  • Spatial selection, filtering, and queries
  • Vector and raster data management
  • GIS data visualization
  • Spatial indexing and query optimization
